findings.action: specCommitment treats a Final Report heading inside a fenced Markdown example as the actual section boundary. Put an unchanged fenced example containing '## 7. Final Report' in Intent, then change a subsequent R1 requirement between the sealed and current revisions: the extracted commitments remain equal. externalDependencyStands permits source reapproval and manifestStandsOver then substitutes the current dependency, preserving consumer approval over changed requirements. This violates R4 and leaves the semantic protection requested by R1-F1 incomplete. Identify the actual Markdown section outside fenced examples and add this negative regression.

The heading expression excludes carriage returns before its multiline end anchor. With CRLF content, '## 7. Final Report\r\n' does not match, so specCommitment compares the entire file. A follow-up disposition change alone therefore rejects a moved dependency despite identical commitment text before the Final Report, violating R1. An in-memory probe using the expression extracted from this source matched the LF heading and failed the CRLF heading. Recognize CRLF boundaries while preserving comparison of commitment content.

GetSpec supports section-split specs, whose Path is their directory (spec.go:487-501). These git show calls consequently read a tree listing rather than the spec's section contents. Observed 'git show 6cd8e2361b4c54b60f9bdbc5d18edbdd593b92ed:.pose/specs' begins with 'tree 6cd8e2361b4c54b60f9bdbc5d18edbdd593b92ed:.pose/specs'; a different revision changes that header, and no Final Report heading exists in the listing. Thus a split dependency cannot retain approval over a moved revision even when only final-report.md changed, contrary to R1. Read and compare the supported split-spec commitment sections at both revisions and cover Final Report-only and requirement changes.
